subject: Error: dynamic index out of bounds

messages.author: 8df77a1c1b1da14e
messages.subject: Error: dynamic index out of bounds
parts:
I have been trying to code a SCR model with an irregular state space, based on the approach presented by Mike Meredith (http://www.mikemeredith.net/blog/1309_SECR_in_JAGS_patchy_habitat.htm). Initially, I got an error when upon execution of nimbleModel(), but that issue when away when I included the habitat matrix as data and explicitly supplied the dimensions, as Perry suggested in another thread (https://groups.google.com/forum/#!topic/nimble-users/BMlWujuX5RE).

So the solution Perry proposed seems to work, inasmuch as the model seems to compile OK, etc. However, when I run CnimMC$run(100), I get the following error:

 

Error in CnimMC$run(100) :
  dynamic index out of bounds: m[trunc(S[i, 1] + 1), trunc(S[i, 2] + 1)]


Here, m is a matrix with dims = nS = c(52,48) . I can't see how the generated index values are ever exceeding these bounds. I'd appreciate any insights about what I'm doing wrong. Hopefully it is something simple. If necessary, I can provide all the R code where I generate data and set up the analysis, etc.

 

Thanks,

Glenn

 

Here is my model:

 

nModel3 <- nimbleCode({
lam0 ~ dgamma(2,1)
psi ~ dunif(0,1)
sig ~ dgamma(2,1)
sig2 <- sig^2

for(i in 1:M){
   w[i] ~ dbern(psi)
   S[i,1] ~ dunif(0, nS[1])
   S[i,2] ~ dunif(0, nS[2])
   #SX[i] <- trunc(S[i,1]+1)
   #SY[i] <- trunc(S[i,2]+1)
   #pOK[i] <- m[SX[i],SY[i]]
   pOK[i] <- m[trunc(S[i,1]+1),trunc(S[i,2]+1)]
   OK[i] ~ dbern(pOK[i]) # OK[i] = 1, the ones trick
   d2[i,1:J] <- pow(S[i,1]-X[1:J,1],2) + pow(S[i,2]-X[1:J,2],2)
   lam[i,1:J] <- lam0*exp(-d2[i,1:J]/sig2/2)
   LAM[i,1:J]<- nT*lam[i,1:J]*w[i]

   for(j in 1:J){
     y[i,j] ~ dpois(LAM[i,j])
   }
}
N <- sum(w[1:M])
})

messages.author: dd632bd3bbcdd7e9
messages.subject: Re: Error: dynamic index out of bounds
parts:
Hi Glenn,

I just saw something like this, so I'm pretty sure the error is occurring because an MCMC sampler such as a random-walk Metropolis-Hastings sampler (which would be used by default on s[i, 1] and s[i, 2]) is proposing values outside the valid range.  Normally these will be rejected because their prior probability is 0 (so log probability is -Inf).  However NIMBLE still attempts to calculate dependent probabilities and in doing so it triggers the error in going outside the valid range of indices in m.  I think we should make a change in NIMBLE to avoid this, maybe by checking at every step of a sequence of model calculations if a -Inf has occurred and bailing out immediately if so.  In the meantime, here are two ways you can avoid the problem.

1. Use "control = list(reflective = TRUE)" as an argument to configureMCMC().   This will make the random-walk MH samplers respect the boundary of the relevant prior.  But it may not help if you experiment with different samplers.

2. Try the following:

SX[i] <- max(0, min(ns[1] - 0.0000001, S[i,1]))
SY[i] <- max(0, min(ns[2] - 0.0000001, S[i,2]))
pOK[i] <- m[trunc(SX[i])+1, trunc(SY[i])+1] 

That builds enforcement of the range of indices for m into the model, so it should be completely general.  Invalid s[i, 1] or s[i, 2] proposals in MCMC will still be rejected due to their prior.

Let us know how it goes.

-Perry

messages.subject: Re: Error: dynamic index out of bounds
parts:
I apologize for bringing this up again, but I have just been revisiting this code again, and I keep getting the following warning (this time it is not an error);

Warning: dynamic index out of bounds: m[trunc(S[i, 1] + 1), trunc(S[i, 2] + 1)]

I tried solution 2 proposed above by Perry, which worked previously without generating any errors or warnings, and which produced sensible results. Now, running the exact same model code, I get the warning (actually, a very long list of identical warnings -related to the number of called iterations). However, the output still seems sensible enough, so I wonder if this warning is just telling me that invalid values were proposed?

The only thing that has changed is that I updated nimble, and I also changed a little bit how I rescale the simulated  trap coordinates to the pixel scale (but the result should be the same, and I also tried it with the original code).
I still suspect that it still is somehow related to how I am creating the mask.

Any thoughts on why this warning is generated (something in nimble, or an error with my code), and how to fix it? I've attached some code (pretty lengthy) that generates a state space, mask, trap array, data, etc, and tries to fit the model.

Thanks,
Glenn

messages.author: 8df77a1c1b1da14e
messages.subject: Re: Error: dynamic index out of bounds
parts:
Ah, I found the mistake, and it is obvious in the warning itself! Apparently I did change the code after all. The offending line:

 pOK[i] <- m[trunc(S[i, 1] + 1), trunc(S[i, 2] + 1)]

should be:
   
 pOK[i] <- m[trunc(SX[i]+1),trunc(SY[i]+1)]

And then it works.

messages.subject: Re: Error: dynamic index out of bounds
parts:
Hello all,

I'm implementing this method from Mike Meredith's website into a SCR model and I'm running into a strange issue. Similar to Glenn, I receive 
Warning: dynamic index out of bounds: habMat[trunc(S[i, 1]), trunc(S[i, 2])].

My code is slightly different and looks more like this:
    S[i,1] ~ dunif(1, upperLimit[1]) # priors for the activity centers for each individual
    S[i,2] ~ dunif(1, upperLimit[2]) # lower x and y coordinates = 1
    pOK[i] <- habMat[trunc(S[i,1]), trunc(S[i,2])]
OK[i] ~ dbern(pOK[i])     # OK[i] = 1, the ones trick

To reduce calculation time, I tweak the values of upperLimit prior to assigning them to constants by subtracting 0.00001. Where upperLimit is a numeric vector with 2 values pertaining to the dimensions of the habitat mask with 1 added. For example, my habitat mask is a matrix with dimensions c(59,42) so the upperLimit values = c(59.99999, 42.99999). 
  In most of the model runs thus far, this has worked great. The most recent run has caused the above warning message to appear. When I look at the values created by the MCMC run, many of them are VERY far outside the min/max values, ie some values areas much/little as -1208451.77.

My question is: Why is the Uniform distribution allowing values to be estimated outside the prescribed min/max provided in S[i,1] ~ dunif(1, upperLimit[1])? 

I see in the previous post that Perry gave a fix, but this creates extra nodes that the model has to calculate, which I want to avoid given that I'm already running into memory issues when compiling the model and long MCMC estimation times. Is there an alternative that would not create extra nodes in the model?

Many thanks,
Colby

And then it works.

messages.author: dd632bd3bbcdd7e9
messages.subject: Re: Error: dynamic index out of bounds
parts:
Hi Colby,

This is somewhat hard to diagnose, partly because it's not a fully reproducible example, and I guess that's because you've described it as an idiosyncratic phenomenon.  The best I can do is give some tips and suggestions.

If it only occurs in some runs, then you could experiment with set.seed(<pick a number>) to find a random number seed that reproduces the problem.  That would give us something to work with.

If the message is generated during nimbleModel(), then it is occurring during uncompiled (i.e. pure R) execution of the model's calculations (and if you don't need that, use calculate=FALSE for a faster model build). That means all R debugging tools are available.  For example you could debug MCMC$run and step through the samplers to look at S[i, 1:2] values as they are updated.  But before diving into that level, you could start by inspecting the model.  Specifically, look at model$S and see if any values are outside of the bounds.  That would indicate some problem with initial values.

In general, nimble tends to be hungrier for valid initial values than is JAGS.  That has to do (at least partly) with default sampler choices.  Are you providing inits for S, and are they definitely valid?

It is also possible that if some other part of the model does not have valid inits, then the initial total log probability (likelihood, if you prefer) is -Inf, in which case some samplers may behave crazily.  You can check with model$getLogProb().  You can check specific parts of the model such as model$getLogProb('S')  (or model$calculate(S), if you've changed any values).

What I suspect is happening with the pathological values in the chain is that once an S[i, 1:2] value gets outside of the valid range, then a sampler will flail and move it around meaninglessly.  If it starts in the valid range, then a move outside the valid range should never be accepted.  That's why I suspect a problem with initial values.

Summary: Setting up a reproducible example is key.  Invalid inits are always worth considering as a cause of basic model problems. 

-Perry
